about: Grace Tyler is one of the few wineries in Oswego County, on the north shore of Oneida Lake in Constantia. Richard and Elizabeth Hamilton bought the land in 2012 and harvested their first grapes in 2017. They opened the winery in 2018 in a building they made largely by hand from aspen poplar grown on the property. It is a small, family-run place: the chocolate Labradors who greet visitors even have a wine named after them.

Chardonnay is a less expected grape this close to Lake Ontario’s snow belt, where most growers rely on cold-hardy hybrids. The winery lists its 2022 Chardonnay as a stainless-steel wine, fermented without new oak. That approach keeps the fruit and the acidity of a cool New York vintage at the center. Steel holds the wine at steady, cool temperatures and shuts out oxygen, so the wine shows the grape and the growing season more than the cellar.

The 2022 shows lemon zest, baked apple and a hint of vanilla. The palate is soft and creamy, with a buttery note, but bright citrus keeps it fresh. It is a gentle, rounded Chardonnay with northern lift. It reads closer to Chablis than to California, and it works well with roast chicken, lake fish, mushrooms and cream sauces.
